https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/f.body: The federal government yesterday defended its proposed $21.7 billion external borrowing plan, insisting that the funds would finance productive investments in infrastructure and other critical sectors to stimulate economic growth, strengthen national productivity and improve living standards. The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said the proposed financing should be assessed based on the assets to be created and the economic returns expected, rather than simply as an addition to the country’s debt burden. Oyedele spoke after the Federal Executive Council (FEC) meeting presided over by President Bola Tinubu at the State House, Abuja, amid criticism of the borrowing plan by former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, as well as the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 election, Peter Obi. Oyedele maintained that the proposal was a financing plan and did not mean the federal government had already borrowed the money or would necessarily draw down the entire amount. “Altogether, if you convert the euro amount and add it to the dollar amount, it will come up to $21.7 billion. First and foremost, this is a plan. It doesn’t mean that we have borrowed. It doesn’t even mean that we borrow all of it. So it’s a plan. The average lifespan of the projects under this plan is five years. This qualifies as investment. This is investment, not borrowing,” Oyedele pointed out. The proposed financing comprises $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion for projects and programmes covering transportation, security, healthcare, agriculture, energy, digital infrastructure, education and social protection. The government said transportation infrastructure accounts for approximately $10.6 billion, including major projects such as the Sokoto-Badagry and Lagos-Calabar highways and the Kano-Kaduna rail project. Oyedele said the government was pursuing financing from multilateral and bilateral development partners, alongside other sources, to implement the projects. Besides, about $7.9 billion is expected from multilateral and bilateral partners, with the World Bank among the major institutions providing support. Oyedele said a $5 billion World Bank component would attract concessional financing at an average interest rate of about 2.1 per cent, while some social-sector loans would carry interest rates of around 2 per cent. He said the government was prioritising favourable financing terms to reduce borrowing costs and ensure that the projects delivered lasting economic benefits. The minister also disclosed that the federal government was targeting single-digit inflation by the end of 2027, as it intensifies efforts to stabilise prices and sustain economic growth. He said inflation had declined to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year, after peaking at about 34 per cent. According to him, FEC resolved to intensify efforts to bring down prices, particularly food prices, while sustaining investments in infrastructure, human capital development and job creation. Oyedele disclosed that Nigeria’s foreign reserves had risen above $55 billion, the highest level in 18 years, while net reserves had increased to more than $45 billion from less than $1 billion three years ago. He put economic growth at 4.43 per cent in the second quarter, compared with 2.74 per cent in May 2023. The minister added that the tax-to-GDP ratio had risen from about seven per cent in 2023 to 12.5 per cent by the end of 2025, while the debt-service-to-revenue ratio had declined from 97 per cent to below 60 per cent. Oyedele also defended the removal of petrol subsidy, arguing that the previous arrangement placed an unsustainable burden on public finances and constrained the government’s ability to invest in infrastructure and essential services. He said Nigeria had increased petrol prices about 3,050 times in 50 years without resolving the underlying subsidy problem, adding that the government had introduced interventions to cushion the impact of economic reforms on vulnerable Nigerians. According to him, more than 10 million households had received over N600 billion in cash transfers, while the Nigerian Education Loan Fund had disbursed N372.6 billion to more than 1.5 million students. He added that more than 800,000 micro, small and medium-sized enterprises had benefited from subsidised loans at single-digit interest rates. The minister further said low-income earners making up to N100,000 monthly were exempt from personal income tax, while businesses with annual turnover of up to N100 million were exempt from corporate income tax, value-added tax and withholding tax under the relevant tax reforms. He also disclosed that the Nigerian capital market had grown from about N30 trillion to more than N160 trillion, expressing optimism about the naira’s outlook on the strength of improved foreign reserves and other economic fundamentals. The federal government also said it was working towards presenting the 2027 budget before the end of the year to allow the National Assembly sufficient time to consider the proposed fiscal framework ahead of the next financial year. The Minister of State for Budget, Doris Uzoka-Anite, disclosed this while briefing journalists after the FEC meeting. “We are working on the 2027 budget, and our intention is to present it before the end of the year,” she said. Further details of the proposed budget, including its overall size, revenue projections, deficit estimates and allocations to key sectors, are expected to emerge as preparations progress. Similarly, the federal government has approved the commencement of procurement for the proposed East and West Super Grids as part of efforts to expand electricity transmission capacity from about 5,000 megawatts to 19,000MW within two years. The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, who disclosed this after the FEC meeting, said the projects would strengthen the national grid and enable more electricity to be transmitted to consumers. He said the government had also approved three major interventions to reinforce transmission infrastructure around Abuja and Lagos, while accelerating efforts to clear more than 300 containers of electricity equipment stranded at the nation’s ports. The first approval covers the construction of a 33kV double-circuit underground and overhead line linked to the Katampe Transmission Substation, which serves the North-Central region. The second involves the design, manufacture and supply of three 300MVA, 330/132/33kV power transformers for the Ikeja West Transmission Substation, a critical facility supplying the Lagos axis. The third project entails the reconstruction and upgrade of the 35.6-kilometre Itumola-Mapasin-Shagamu 132kV single-circuit transmission line to a double-circuit line to accommodate rising electricity demand along the Lagos-Shagamu corridor. Tegbe said the projects formed part of the government’s broader strategy to improve transmission infrastructure, stabilise electricity supply and maximise the use of existing power-sector assets. He disclosed that the ministry had commenced a nationwide technical audit of electricity infrastructure, dividing the country into three major energy zones: Lagos and its surrounding industrial corridor; the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano axis; and the Enugu-Onitsha-Benin axis. According to him, the audit, which began four weeks ago, would identify ageing and weak infrastructure requiring replacement or rehabilitation to improve the reliability of the national grid. The minister also restated that the government had paid N1.23 trillion out of the N3.3 trillion owed to gas suppliers and other stakeholders, adding that the outstanding liabilities had contributed to difficulties in ensuring adequate gas supply to power generation companies. He said the government was working to improve the operational efficiency of the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) and the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) particularly in coordinating grid management and infrastructure development. Tegbe explained that separating system operations from transmission infrastructure management was intended to improve efficiency, response times and coordination across the electricity network. He added that the government was reviewing options for greater private-sector participation in electricity asset management to improve performance and ensure better utilisation of existing infrastructure. On the super grids, Tegbe said the projects would strengthen transmission links across the northern and southern parts of the country, connecting Sokoto through Abuja and other locations to parts of the South. He said Tinubu had approved the commencement of the procurement process, describing the initiative as a significant step towards building a more resilient electricity network capable of supporting future demand. Tegbe also announced that construction had commenced on a new National Control Centre (NCC) in Osogbo to replace the existing facility, which he said was built 64 years ago. The new centre is expected to strengthen the monitoring and management of the national grid. He further disclosed that the government was energising completed transmission substations in Kano, Katsina, Bauchi and Gombe, among other locations, to bring idle infrastructure into service. The minister said the government was also expanding access to electricity through solar mini-grids, particularly in institutions and locations facing transmission constraints. According to him, at least 14 federal universities had received installed and energised solar mini-grids, with capacities ranging from one megawatt to five megawatts. Another 11 universities were being supported through the Tertiary Education Trust Fund, bringing the number of institutions covered by the programme to nearly 30. He stated that five teaching hospitals were also benefiting from solar power installations being implemented in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health. On the backlog of electricity equipment stranded at the ports, Tegbe described the situation as unacceptable, saying some containers had reportedly remained uncleared for between 14 and 20 years. He said the president had directed the ministry to work with the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) and the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) to clear more than 300 containers containing electricity equipment. Tegbe attributed the prolonged delay to the failure of previous administrations to settle outstanding charges and complete the necessary clearance processes. In the same vein, FEC has approved N45.8 billion for a biosecurity and disease surveillance system at five international airports to strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to detect Ebola and other dangerous pathogens at its borders. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Ali Pate, disclosed this after the meeting, saying the project would be implemented under a 20-year public-private partnership concession awarded to BioHealth Consortium following the council’s approval of its full business case. Pate described the initiative as a major investment in Nigeria’s health and economic security, warning that infectious disease outbreaks could disrupt economic activities and threaten public safety. “Over the last two weeks, I think you realise the significance of enhancing biosecurity at our points of entry. Since COVID, we have known that there are significant vulnerabilities in terms of public health threats crossing borders and the need for coordinated, technology-driven systems for early warning, detection and response to emerging infectious disease threats,” he stressed. The surveillance system will be deployed at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos; Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja; Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport, Kano; Port Harcourt International Airport; and Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/f.title_zh: 联邦政府为217亿美元贷款辩护，称资金将用于生产性项目
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/f.body_zh: 联邦政府昨日为其拟议的217亿美元外债融资方案辩护，坚持表示，这笔资金将用于基础设施及其他关键部门的生产性投资，以刺激经济增长、增强国家生产力并改善生活水平。财政部长兼经济协调部长Taiwo Oyedele表示，评估拟议融资方案时，应依据将要创造的资产和预期经济回报，而不应仅将其视为国家债务负担的增加。Oyedele是在总统Bola Tinubu于阿布贾国家宫主持的联邦执行委员会（FEC）会议后发表上述言论的。当时，前副总统Atiku Abubakar，以及参加2027年选举的尼日利亚民主党（NDC）总统候选人Peter Obi均对该融资方案提出批评。Oyedele坚称，该提案是一项融资计划，并不意味着联邦政府已经借入了这笔资金，也不意味着政府必然会提取全部金额。他说：“总体而言，如果把欧元金额折算后加到美元金额上，总额将达到217亿美元。首先，这是一项计划。这不意味着我们已经借了钱，甚至不意味着我们会借入全部资金。因此，这是一项计划。该计划下项目的平均实施周期为五年。这符合投资性质。这是投资，不是借款。”Oyedele指出，拟议融资包括205.2亿美元和10.45亿欧元，用于交通、安全、医疗卫生、农业、能源、数字基础设施、教育和社会保护领域的项目与计划。政府表示，交通基础设施约占106亿美元，包括Sokoto-Badagry和Lagos-Calabar高速公路以及Kano-Kaduna铁路项目等重大工程。Oyedele说，政府正寻求多边和双边发展伙伴及其他来源的融资，以实施这些项目。此外，预计约79亿美元将来自多边和双边伙伴，世界银行是提供支持的主要机构之一。Oyedele表示，世界银行提供的50亿美元部分将获得优惠融资，平均利率约为2.1%，部分社会领域贷款的利率约为2%。他说，政府正优先争取有利的融资条件，以降低借贷成本，并确保项目带来持久的经济效益。部长还透露，随着政府加大力度稳定物价并维持经济增长，联邦政府的目标是在2027年底前将通胀率降至个位数。他说，通胀率已从此前一度达到约34%的峰值降至9月的14.63%，而上年同期为20.98%。据他介绍，FEC决定加大力度压低物价，尤其是食品价格，同时维持对基础设施、人力资源开发和就业创造的投入。Oyedele透露，尼日利亚外汇储备已升至550亿美元以上，达到18年来最高水平；净储备也由三年前不足10亿美元增至逾450亿美元。他表示，第二季度经济增长率为4.43%，相比之下，2023年5月为2.74%。部长补充称，税收占国内生产总值的比率已从2023年的约7%升至2025年底的12.5%，而偿债占收入比率则从97%降至60%以下。Oyedele还为取消汽油补贴辩护，认为此前的安排给公共财政造成不可持续的重负，并限制政府投资基础设施和基本服务的能力。他说，尼日利亚在50年间约3,050次上调汽油价格，却未能解决潜在的补贴问题；政府还推出干预措施，以缓冲经济改革对脆弱的尼日利亚人造成的影响。据他介绍，超过1,000万户家庭已获得逾6,000亿奈拉现金转移支付，尼日利亚教育贷款基金也已向逾150万名学生发放3,726亿奈拉。他补充说，超过80万家微型企业、小型和中型企业获得了低个位数利率的补贴贷款。部长进一步表示，根据相关税收改革改革，月收入不超过10万奈拉的低收入者免征个人所得税，年营业额不超过1亿奈拉的企业免征企业所得税、增值税和预提税。他还透露，尼日利亚资本市场已从约30万亿奈拉增至逾160万亿奈拉，并对奈拉前景表示乐观，理由是外汇储备及其他经济基本面有所改善。联邦政府还表示，正努力在年底前提交2027年度预算，以便为国民议会留出充足时间，在下一财政年度开始前审议拟议财政框架。预算国务部长Doris Uzoka-Anite在FEC会议后向记者介绍情况时说：“我们正在制定2027年度预算，计划在年底前提交。”随着准备工作推进，拟议预算的更多细节，包括总体规模、收入预测、赤字估算以及向重点领域的拨款，预计将陆续公布。同样，联邦政府已批准启动拟议东部和西部超级电网的采购工作，努力在两年内将输电能力从约5,000兆瓦提升至19,000MW。电力部长Joseph Tegbe在FEC会议后透露此事，并表示这些项目将强化国家电网，使更多电力能够输送给消费者。他说，政府还批准了加强阿布贾和拉各斯周边输电基础设施的三项重大干预措施，同时加快清理滞留在全国各港口的300多个电力设备集装箱。第一项批准涉及建设一条与Katampe输电变电站相连的33kV双回路地下及架空线路，该变电站服务于中北部地区。第二项涉及为Ikeja West输电变电站设计、制造和供应三台300MVA、330/132/33kV电力变压器，该设施是向拉各斯轴线供电的关键设施。第三个项目包括将35.6公里的Itumola-Mapasin-Shagamu 132kV单回路输电线路重建并升级为双回路线路，以满足Lagos-Shagamu走廊不断增长的用电需求。Tegbe表示，这些项目是政府改善输电基础设施、稳定电力供应并最大限度利用现有电力行业资产整体战略的一部分。他透露，电力部已启动全国电力基础设施技术审计，将全国划分为三大能源区：拉各斯及其周边工业走廊；Abuja-Kaduna-Kano轴线；以及Enugu-Onitsha-Benin轴线。据他介绍，审计于四周前启动，将确定需要更换或修复的老化和薄弱基础设施，以提高国家电网可靠性。部长还重申，政府已从欠付天然气供应商及其他利益相关方的3.3万亿奈拉中支付了1.23万亿奈拉，并指出未偿债务导致难以确保向发电公司供应充足天然气。他说，政府正努力提高尼日利亚输电公司（TCN）和尼日利亚独立系统运营商（NISO）的运营效率，尤其是在电网管理和基础设施开发方面的协调能力。Tegbe解释，将系统运营与输电基础设施管理分开，旨在提高整个电力网络的效率、响应速度和协调水平。他补充说，政府正在研究扩大私营部门参与电力资产管理、提高绩效并确保现有基础设施得到更充分利用的方案。关于超级电网，Tegbe表示，这些项目将加强尼日利亚南北部之间的输电联系，把Sokoto经阿布贾及其他地点与南部部分地区连接起来。他说，Tinubu已批准启动采购程序，并将这项倡议描述为建设更具韧性的电力网络、使其能够支撑未来用电需求的重要一步。Tegbe还宣布，位于奥索博博的新国家控制中心（NCC）已经开工，将取代现有设施；据他说，现有设施建于64年前。新中心预计将加强国家电网的监控与管理。他还透露，政府正在为Kano、Katsina、Bauchi和Gombe等地的已完工输电变电站通电，使闲置基础设施投入运行。部长表示，政府还通过太阳能微电网扩大电力供应范围，特别是在面临输电限制的机构和地区。据他介绍，至少14所联邦大学已安装并接入太阳能微电网，容量从1兆瓦至5兆瓦不等。另有11所大学正通过高等教育信托基金获得支持，使该计划覆盖的机构总数增至近30所。他表示，五家教学医院也将受益于与联邦卫生部合作实施的太阳能发电设施。在滞留在港口的电力设备积压问题上，Tegbe称这一状况“不可接受”，并表示据报道一些集装箱已有14年至20年未获清关。他说，总统已指示该部与尼日利亚港务局（NPA）及尼日利亚海关总署（NCS）合作，清运300多个装有电力设备的集装箱。Tegbe将长期延误归咎于历届政府未能缴清未付费用并完成必要的清关程序。与此同时，FEC已批准为五个国际机场的生物安全和疾病监测系统拨款458亿奈拉，以加强尼日利亚在边境发现埃博拉及其他危险病原体的能力。卫生与社会福利协调部长Ali Pate教授在会后透露，该项目将根据一项为期20年的公私合作伙伴特许安排实施；内阁批准BioHealth Consortium的完整商业计划后，该特许权已授予该财团。Pate称，这项倡议是对尼日利亚卫生和经济安全的重大投资，并警告说，传染病暴发可能扰乱经济活动并威胁公众安全。他强调：“过去两周，我认为大家已经意识到加强入境口岸生物安全的重要性。自COVID以来，我们就知道，公共卫生威胁跨境传播方面存在重大脆弱性，也需要协调一致、由技术驱动的系统，对新出现的传染病威胁进行预警、检测和响应。”该监测系统将部署于拉各斯Murtala Muhammed国际机场、阿布贾Nnamdi Azikiwe国际机场、Kano的Mallam Aminu Kano国际机场、Port Harcourt国际机场以及Enugu的Akanu Ibiam国际机场。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/t.title: TUC Rejects FG’s N70,000 Transport Allowance, Demands Salary Increase
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/t.summary: Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) yesterday objected to the federal government’s proposed N70,000 transport allowance to civil servants, saying temporary wage awards are not sustainable and far-reaching. The federal government had approved a monthly transport allowance of N70,000 for public service workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, to cushion the effects of rising living costs.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/t.summary_zh: 尼日利亚工会大会（TUC）昨日反对联邦政府拟向公务员发放每月N70,000交通津贴，称临时性加薪奖励不可持续，也难以长期推行。联邦政府已批准自2026年11月起，为各级公共服务人员连续6个月每月发放N70,000交通津贴，以缓解生活成本上涨带来的影响。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/t.body: Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) yesterday objected to the federal government’s proposed N70,000 transport allowance to civil servants, saying temporary wage awards are not sustainable and far-reaching. The objection came as former Vice President and presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, described the N70,000 monthly transport support for public service workers as a desperate last-minute attempt to contain public anger. The federal government had approved a monthly transport allowance of N70,000 for public service workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, to cushion the effects of rising living costs. The approval was announced in a memorandum of understanding (MoU) issued at the end of a conciliation meeting between government representatives and leaders of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) in Abuja on Tuesday. The MoU was signed by Tanimu Yakubu, Director-General of the budget office; Joe Ajaero, NLC President; Garba Abdul, Permanent Secretary of the Service Welfare Office in the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation; and Muhammad Dingyadi, Minister of Labour and Employment. However, TUC demanded immediate salary increase for workers and implementation of agreement reached with Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU). TUC said its position was taken at its National Administrative Council meeting on October 8 in Abuja, where it sent a demand letter to the federal government through the office of Secretary to Government of the Federation. A statement signed by TUC President, Festus Osifo, said the union would await the outcome of a meeting with the federal government to decide on the next steps to take. The congress said the letter was in furtherance of an earlier press briefing on the economic hardship facing workers and proposed measures to address it. On salary increase, TUC said its position was clear that the federal government should review and increase the salaries of workers. It said the government did not require any minimum wage negotiation before increasing pay, as there was no maximum wage law in the country. It stated that some states had raised minimum wage above N100,000, adding that the federal government could raise the pay of its lowest workers to N300,000, from the current N70,000, and apply consequential adjustment. “While it is good to negotiate minimum wage, which will affect other cadre of workers, FGN must raise wage level immediately as there are no law or historical practices stopping it from doing so,” TUC stated. Following the letter, the TUC leadership held consultative meetings with government officials, including Secretary to Government of Federation, where its position was canvassed. It said the proposal of wage award was mentioned, but it was vehemently rejected for several reasons. According to TUC, temporary wage awards are not sustainable and far-reaching. The congress cited the wage award agreed on October 2, 2023, which was to be implemented until the minimum wage was agreed in 2024, but was never implemented holistically, with some workers still owed one or two months while others never received it. TUC stated, “How do we go back to same wage award that never benefited all workers? How can workers be expected to trust fresh promises when previous obligations remain outstanding?” It also cited irregularity in the payment of the 2023 wage award, where those who got up to four months of N40,000 never got it monthly but at intervals, while over 80 per cent of states and the informal sector never implemented any wage award. “From the foregoing, we further reiterate our demand for pay raise for all government workers, as salary is only consistent and far-reaching pay that workers could rely upon,” TUC said. It stressed that negotiations of a new national minimum wage must not become an excuse for postponing urgent pay increment. On cost-of-living relief, TUC said economic crisis affected not only federal workers but also state and local government workers, as well as pensioners, private sector and informal economy workers. It called on government at all levels to implement measurable interventions to reduce the cost of essential goods, ensure timely payment of salaries and pensions, and revitalise the productive sector. On JOHESU, Osifo said he led the organised labour team that included the JOHESU leadership to resolve the industrial action that lasted several months. He said after several meetings at the Federal Ministry of Health, a final conciliatory meeting was held at Ministry of Labour and Employment, where a communique was agreed. The signing led to suspension of the industrial action in good faith, but TUC said the government did not keep its side. Under the terms of settlement, it was agreed that all outstanding issues relating to CONHESS adjustment shall be conclusively addressed without further delay, but seven months later, adjustment remained unimplemented, Osifo said. “This continued failure to honour explicit commitment violates principle of good faith, undermines confidence in collective bargaining, and is absolutely unacceptable,” the TUC said. It demanded immediate implementation of CONHESS adjustment, clear timetable, budgetary provisions, and resolution of outstanding matters. TUC said its position was unequivocal that workers were demanding social and economic justice, adding that it would defend workers’ rights without retreat and pursue every legitimate avenue to compel government to honour obligations. It said it awaited the final outcome of scheduled meetings with the government to decide the next line of action. Meanwhile, Atiku condemned the N70,000 monthly transport support for public service workers as a desperate attempt by the federal government to contain public anger. He said it was an admittance that government policies had made life unbearable for millions of citizens. In a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said, “The Tinubu administration is scrambling from one announcement to another, showing its failure to grasp the crisis. The cost-of-living crisis reaches beyond transport: energy, food, rent and other essentials affect every part of daily life. “Barbers pay more to power their clippers; restaurant owners face higher cooking costs; shopkeepers struggle to keep prices down; school bus operators pay more for fuel; and families still must buy food. Every business and household are affected. Does hardship end at the bus stop?” The statement said, “If public service workers receive N70,000 monthly for transport from November, what happens to private sector workers, traders, small businesses, transport operators and millions without formal jobs? The public workforce is only a fraction of Nigeria’s population. A temporary allowance for some cannot solve a national crisis. “The agreement also leaves the effective date for a new minimum wage unresolved. The government must publish payment dates, explain eligibility and say when wage negotiations will produce a decision.” Atiku said, “Any genuine relief is welcome, but a six-month allowance cannot undo this hardship. At about N1,400 per litre, N70,000 buys roughly 50 litres of petrol. What meaningful difference can 50 litres make over an entire month? “What Nigerians are witnessing is a government that set the house ablaze with its reckless policies, then pretends to fight the inferno by throwing ice cubes at the flames. A temporary N70,000 allowance cannot extinguish a cost-of-living crisis this government ignited. “This is the pattern: the fuel discount failed, the 90-day cost of living plan failed before it began, and now comes another temporary payment. The government promised CNG would lower transport costs, but that promise has failed. For Nigerians still paying more to commute, the CNG programme is another scam of promises, while families face the same unaffordable prices.” The statement added, “These rushed announcements smack of political bribery and corruption. Tinubu has shown no genuine intention of clearing the monumental mess caused by his hasty subsidy removal. He offers temporary payments instead of confronting the consequences. “Atiku has proposed a practical alternative: a transparently managed production subsidy for fuel refined in Nigeria, delivering relief at the pump. Tinubu must not punish 250 million Nigerians for the corruption and leakages of a few thousand. His arrogance prevents him from reconsidering a cocky decision, while families and businesses pay the price. “N70,000 may help with transport, but it cannot explain why work, food and running a business have become unaffordable. Nigerians need lasting relief, decent wages and an economy that rewards honest work. When will life become affordable again?” Atiku said his campaign would pursue practical measures to lower living costs, raise household incomes, and restore dignity to work. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/t.title_zh: 工会大会拒绝联邦政府发放的70,000奈拉交通津贴，要求提高工资
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/t.body_zh: 尼日利亚工会大会（TUC）昨天反对联邦政府拟向公务员发放N70,000交通津贴，称临时性加薪措施既不可持续，也无法带来广泛持久的效果。反对之际，非洲民主大会（ADC）前副总统兼总统候选人阿蒂库·阿布巴卡尔将每月向公共服务人员提供的N70,000交通补贴描述为联邦政府为平息公众愤怒而作出的绝望的最后努力。联邦政府已批准自2026年11月起，连续六个月向各级公共服务人员每月发放N70,000交通津贴，以缓解生活成本上涨的影响。该批准是在政府代表与尼日利亚劳工大会（NLC）领导人周二于阿布贾举行的调解会议结束时签署的一份谅解备忘录（MoU）中公布的。谅解备忘录由预算办公室主任塔尼穆·亚库布、NLC主席乔·阿贾埃罗、联邦公务员首长办公室公务员福利办公室常任秘书加尔巴·阿卜杜勒，以及劳工与就业部长穆罕马德·丁亚迪签署。然而，TUC要求立即为工人加薪，并落实与联合卫生部门工会（JOHESU）达成的协议。TUC表示，其立场是在10月8日于阿布贾举行的全国行政委员会会议上确定的，并在会上通过联邦政府秘书办公室向联邦政府递交了一份要求信。TUC主席费斯图斯·奥西福签署的声明称，该工会将等待与联邦政府会议的结果，再决定下一步行动。工会大会表示，这封信是对此前有关工人面临经济困境及拟议应对措施的新闻简报的进一步跟进。关于加薪，TUC表示其立场十分明确，即联邦政府应重新审查并提高工人薪酬。TUC称，政府在提高薪酬前无须进行任何最低工资谈判，因为该国没有最高工资法。TUC指出，一些州已将最低工资提高至N100,000以上，并补充说，联邦政府可以把最低级别工人的薪酬从目前的N70,000提高到N300,000，同时实行连带调整。TUC称：“协商最低工资固然重要，因为这将影响其他类别的工作人员，但联邦政府必须立即提高工资水平，因为没有任何法律或历史惯例阻止其这样做。”递交信件后，TUC领导层与包括联邦政府秘书在内的政府官员举行磋商会议，向他们阐明自身立场。TUC表示，会上提到了加薪方案，但该方案因若干理由遭到强烈反对。据TUC称，临时加薪措施既不可持续，也难以产生广泛持久的效果。工会大会援引了2023年10月2日商定的加薪方案，该方案原定实施至2024年确定最低工资之日，但从未得到全面落实；一些工人仍被拖欠一至两个月工资，另一些人则从未领到这笔工资。TUC称：“我们怎能再次回到那个从未让所有工人受益的加薪方案？在先前的义务仍未履行的情况下，我们怎能指望工人相信新的承诺？”TUC还指出，2023年加薪方案在发放过程中存在不规律现象；有些工人最多可领取四个月、每月N40,000的加薪，但款项并非按月发放，而是间隔发放；超过80%的州和非正规部门则从未落实任何加薪方案。TUC表示：“鉴于上述情况，我们再次重申要求提高所有政府工作人员薪酬，因为薪酬是唯一稳定持久、能够信赖的报酬。”TUC强调，协商新的全国最低工资绝不能成为推迟紧急加薪的借口。在缓解生活成本压力方面，TUC表示，经济危机不仅影响联邦政府工作人员，也影响州和地方政府工作人员、退休金领取者、私营部门及非正规经济从业者。TUC呼吁各级政府采取可衡量的干预措施，降低 essentials等基本商品的成本，确保按时支付工资和退休金，并振兴生产部门。关于JOHESU，奥西福表示，他曾率领包括JOHESU领导层在内的劳工团队，解决了持续数月的行业行动。他说，在联邦卫生部举行多次会议后，劳工与就业部又举行了最后一次调解会议，各方就一份联合公报达成一致。签署公报促使行业行动出于善意而暂停，但TUC表示政府没有履行自己的义务。根据和解条款，所有与CONHESS调整有关的未决问题都应立即得到最终处理，但七个月后，该调整仍未落实。奥西福说：“这种持续不履行明确承诺的行为违反善意原则，削弱人们对集体谈判的信心，绝对不可接受。”TUC要求立即落实CONHESS调整、明确时间表、安排预算资金，并解决所有遗留问题。TUC表示，其立场毫不含糊，即工人正在争取社会和经济正义，并将坚定不移地捍卫工人权利，采取一切合法途径迫使政府履行义务。TUC称，将等待与政府既定会议的最后结果，再决定后续行动。与此同时，阿蒂库谴责每月向公共服务人员提供N70,000交通补贴，称这是联邦政府为平息公众愤怒而作出的绝望努力。他说，这等于承认政府政策已令数百万公民的生活难以忍受。ADC总统竞选委员会战略传播主任弗兰克·沙伊布发布声明称，阿蒂库表示：“蒂努布政府仓促地从一个公告转向另一个公告，表明其未能把握这场危机。生活成本危机不只涉及交通：能源、食物、房租及其他生活必需品影响着日常生活的每个方面。“理发师为电动理发器供电需要支付更多费用；餐馆老板面临更高的烹饪成本；店主努力维持较低售价；校车运营商支付更多燃油费；家庭依然需要购买食物。每一家企业和每一个家庭都受到影响。困难难道到公交站就结束了吗？”声明称：“如果公共服务人员从11月起每月获得N70,000交通补贴，私营部门工人、商贩、小企业、运输运营商以及数以百万计没有正式工作的人又该怎么办？公共部门工作人员只占尼日利亚人口的一小部分。向部分人员发放临时津贴，无法解决全国性危机。“该协议也没有确定新最低工资的生效日期。政府必须公布支付日期，说明资格条件，并说明工资协商何时能产生结果。”阿蒂库说：“任何真正有意义的纾困措施都值得欢迎，但六个月的津贴无法消除这些困难。在每升约N1,400的价格下，N70,000大约只能买50升汽油。整整一个月里，50升汽油能带来多大实际意义？“尼日利亚人目睹的是一个因鲁莽政策纵火烧掉自家、随后又假装通过向火焰扔冰块来扑灭大火的政府。每月N70,000的临时津贴无法熄灭本届政府亲手引发的这场生活成本危机。“这就是一贯的做法：燃油折扣失败了，90天生活成本计划尚未启动就已失败，现在又来了一笔临时付款。政府承诺压缩天然气将降低交通成本，但这一承诺已经落空。对仍在通勤中支付更高费用的尼日利亚人而言，压缩天然气计划不过是又一个骗局般的承诺，而家庭仍面对同样难以承受的价格。”声明补充道：“这些仓促发布的公告带有政治贿赂和腐败的味道。蒂努布没有表现出任何真正意图去处理其草率取消补贴所造成的严重烂摊子。他宁愿提供临时款项，也不愿面对取消补贴的后果。“阿蒂库提出了一项切实可行的替代方案：对在尼日利亚炼制的燃油实行透明管理的生产补贴，在加油站直接向消费者提供纾困。蒂努布不能因为少数人的腐败和流失，让2.5亿尼日利亚人受罚。他的傲慢使他无法重新考虑这个傲慢的决定，而家庭和企业却在为此买单。“N70,000或许有助于交通支出，但它无法解释为何工作、食物和经营企业都变得难以负担。尼日利亚人需要持久而有效的纾困、体面的工资，以及一个让诚实劳动获得回报的经济。生活在何时才能重新变得负担得起？”阿蒂库表示，他的竞选团队将推动切实措施，降低生活成本，提高家庭收入，并恢复劳动的尊严。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/a.summary: • Senate President expresses optimism over decentralised policing •Urges northern youths to mobilise support for Tinubu’s 2027 re-election President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, on Wednesday disclosed that about 30 state Houses of Assembly had endorsed the proposed constitution amendment to establish state police.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/a.summary_zh: • 参议院议长对推行分散式警务表示乐观 • 敦促北部青年动员支持蒂努布在2027年再次参选 参议院议长戈德斯威尔·阿卡皮奥周三表示，已有约30个州议会赞同拟议的宪法修正案，以建立州级警察制度。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/a.body: • Senate President expresses optimism over decentralised policing •Urges northern youths to mobilise support for Tinubu’s 2027 re-election President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, on Wednesday disclosed that about 30 state Houses of Assembly had endorsed the proposed constitution amendment to establish state police. Akpabio expressed optimism that Nigeria could soon adopt a decentralised policing system to strengthen national security. He spoke when members of Arewa Revival Project, a northern youth organisation with membership across the 19 northern states, visited him at his office in Abuja. The senate president said the proposed reform would improve the country’s capacity to tackle insecurity by bringing policing closer to communities. He expressed confidence that the constitution amendment process was nearing completion, adding that the establishment of state police would complement existing security structures and enhance efforts to address the country’s security challenges. He urged the youth to intensify grassroots mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, stating that continuity in government would allow the administration’s economic reforms and security policies to produce the desired results. Akpabio also called on the Nigerian youth to rise above what he described as paid social media propaganda against the administration. He said the president had taken significant steps to diversify the economy, reform the tax system, and address longstanding structural problems. The senate president expressed optimism that Nigeria would overcome its security challenges, urging the youth to remain confident in the country’s future while supporting efforts to restore peace and stability. He stated, “I always tell them that the devil that you see today, you will soon see them no more. Very soon, we shall overcome the insecurity that we face today. So, feel confident as you go round campaigning.” Akpabio maintained that decentralised policing would further strengthen national security, particularly by improving the ability of law enforcement agencies to respond to threats within their respective communities. He urged the Arewa youths to mobilise support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election, saying the administration needs time to consolidate its policies. He said the president had taken steps to move Nigeria away from its longstanding dependence on crude oil revenues and introduce reforms intended to reposition the economy. He said, “I expect the Nigerian youth to rise above social media propaganda because this president has managed to take us out of a mono-economy, an economy that was dependent only on crude oil. Akpabio stated that the administration’s performance had earned it the support of the National Assembly, declaring that lawmakers have endorsed Tinubu for a second term. He said, “No president has achieved the level of development that he has done in this country today since independence. The naysayers will not want to say so, but I am very proud and members of the National Assembly are very proud. Akpabio said Nigeria’s continued survival amid economic and security difficulties reflected the president’s willingness to confront the challenges facing the country. “I give glory to God that Nigeria is still surviving, and surviving because we have a president who thinks and somebody who wants to face challenges, and he is facing the challenges,” he said. He urged the youth to support continuity in government, stating that changing the administration before its policies fully matures could undermine the progress made so far. He stated, “You don’t change a winning team. He is doing so well. Allow his policies to crystallise. This is not somebody who is coming to experiment. He is already doing it.” Akpabio also emphasised the importance of youth participation in national development, saying government policies should create a stable foundation for future generations. He said, “Whatever we are doing today, we are doing it to stabilise your future and ensure the survival of Nigeria. So, it is good that you are seeing it.” He warned that the youth could face considerable challenges in countering criticism of the administration on social media, alleging that some individuals attacking the president and his supporters online are being paid to do so. Akpabio alleged, “It is not going to be easy for you because most of those who are attacking the president and attacking these young men on social media are being paid. You are not being paid.” He advised the youth to organise periodic grassroots engagements to explain government policies and challenge misinformation, rather than attempt to compete continuously with critics on social media. He said, “You may not be able to have the kind of energy and time with them. But once in a while, gather the youth together and let them see the truth and know the truth.” The visit provided an opportunity for the Arewa Revival Project to express support for Akpabio’s leadership of the National Assembly and recognise what it described as his contributions to national development. Earlier, Project Coordinator, Arewa Revival Project, Hon. Mustafa Ibrahim, said the organisation considered Akpabio deserving of recognition because of his contributions to nation-building and the achievements recorded under his leadership of the National Assembly. The group, whose membership spans the 19 northern states, presented the senate president with an award in recognition of his contributions to national development. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/a.title_zh: 阿卡比奥：已有30个州支持为州警察制度修改宪法
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/a.body_zh:
• 尼日利亚参议院议长对推行权力下放式警务表示乐观，敦促北部青年动员支持 Tinubu 2027年连任
参议院议长 Godswill Akpabio 周三透露，约有30个州议会赞成拟议的宪法修正案，以设立州警察。Akpabio 表示乐观，认为尼日利亚很快就能采用权力下放式警务制度，从而加强国家安全。当天，成员遍及北部19个州的青年组织 Arewa Revival Project 到办公室拜访他，会面地点位于阿布贾。

参议院议长表示，拟议中的改革将让警务更贴近社区，从而提升国家应对不安全局势的能力。他确信宪法修正程序即将完成，并补充说，设立州警察将补充现有安全架构，增强应对国家安全挑战的努力。

他敦促青年加强基层动员，支持总统 Bola Tinubu 在2027年再次参选，称政府延续执政将使本届政府的经济改革和安全政策取得预期成果。Akpabio 还呼吁尼日利亚青年超越他所说的针对本届政府的付费社交媒体宣传。他表示，总统已经采取重要举措，推动经济多元化、改革税收制度，并处理长期存在的结构性问题。

参议院议长乐观地表示，尼日利亚将克服安全挑战，并敦促青年继续相信国家未来，同时支持恢复和平与稳定的努力。他说：“我总是告诉他们，今天你们看到的魔鬼，很快就会再也见不到。很快，我们就会克服当前面临的不安全局势。因此，你们四处开展竞选活动时，务必保持信心。”

Akpabio 坚持认为，权力下放式警务将进一步强化国家安全，尤其是提升执法机构应对各自社区内威胁的能力。他敦促 Arewa 青年在2027年总统选举前动员支持 Tinubu，并表示本届政府需要时间巩固各项政策。

他说，总统已经采取措施，使尼日利亚摆脱长期以来对原油收入的依赖，并推行旨在重塑经济地位的改革。他说：“我期待尼日利亚青年能够超越社交媒体上的宣传，因为这位总统已经带领我们摆脱单一经济，也就是一种只依赖原油的经济。”

Akpabio 表示，本届政府的表现赢得了国民议会的支持，并宣称议员们已经支持 Tinubu 连任。他说：“自独立以来，还没有哪位总统在这个国家取得他今天所达到的发展水平。唱反调者不愿承认这一点，但我非常自豪，国民议会成员也都非常自豪。”

Akpabio 表示，尼日利亚在经济与安全困境中依然存续，体现了总统愿意正面应对国家所面临挑战的决心。他说：“我感谢上帝，尼日利亚依然存续，而且之所以能够存续，是因为我们拥有一位会思考、愿意面对挑战的总统，而他正在迎接这些挑战。”

他敦促青年支持政府延续执政，并表示，如果在本届政府政策尚未完全成熟之前更迭政府，就可能削弱迄今取得的进展。他说：“不要更换一支正在获胜的队伍。他的表现如此出色。让他的政策充分成型。这不是一个前来试验的人。他已经在付诸实践。”

Akpabio 还强调青年参与国家发展的重要性，表示政府政策应为后代建立稳定的基础。他说：“我们今天所做的一切，都是为了让你们的未来更加稳定，并确保尼日利亚得以存续。因此，你们现在看到这些成果是好事。”

他警告称，青年在反驳社交媒体上对本届政府的批评时可能面临巨大困难，并指称一些在网上攻击总统及其支持者的人正因此获得报酬。Akpabio 指控说：“这对你们来说不会容易，因为大多数在社交媒体上攻击总统和这些年轻人的人都是拿钱办事。而你们没有拿钱。”

他建议青年定期组织基层交流活动，解释政府政策并反驳错误信息，而不是试图在社交媒体上持续与批评者竞争。他说：“你们或许无法投入他们那样的精力和时间。但可以偶尔召集青年，让大家看到真相、认识真相。”

此次拜访让 Arewa Revival Project 有机会表达对 Akpabio 领导国民议会的支持，并认可其所称的 Akpabio 对国家发展的贡献。此前，Arewa Revival Project 项目协调员 Hon. Mustafa Ibrahim 表示，该组织认为 Akpabio 对国家建设作出的贡献，以及其在领导国民议会期间取得的成就，足以令其获得表彰。这个成员遍及北部19个州的团体向参议院议长颁发了奖项，以表彰他对国家发展的贡献。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/m.title: Minister: Tinubu’s Reforms Yielding Results, More Gains Expected
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/m.summary: The Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajiya Imaan Sulaiman Ibrahim, has defended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s economic reforms, describing them as necessary and bold decisions that are beginning to deliver results despite the economic difficulties faced by Nigerians.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/m.summary_zh: 妇女事务与社会发展部长Hajiya Imaan Sulaiman Ibrahim为President Bola Ahmed Tinubu的经济改革辩护，称这些改革是必要且大胆的决定，尽管尼日利亚人面临经济困难，但相关举措已开始取得成效。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/m.body: The Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajiya Imaan Sulaiman Ibrahim, has defended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s economic reforms, describing them as necessary and bold decisions that are beginning to deliver results despite the economic difficulties faced by Nigerians. Sulaiman-Ibrahim stated this on Tuesday at a national press conference organised ahead of the unveiling of a book examining Tinubu’s reform agenda. She said the president had chosen to confront the country’s longstanding economic problems rather than transfer the burden to future generations. The book, titled The Courage to Reform: Architecture of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR – Beyond 2027: Statecraft, Vision for National Renewal, is being promoted by the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement to showcase the administration’s policies and achievements over the past three years. According to the minister, Tinubu assumed office on May 29, 2023, amid difficult economic circumstances that demanded decisive action to address structural weaknesses in Nigeria’s economy, revenue collection system and public finances. She explained the petrol subsidy was consuming funds that could otherwise have been invested in essential public services, including education, healthcare and road infrastructure. She also criticised the existing tax system for placing disproportionate pressure on the people it was meant to protect. “When Mr. President took the oath of office on 29 May 2023, he inherited hard choices that could no longer wait. A petrol subsidy was draining the resources meant for our schools, our hospitals and our roads and our tax system weighed most heavily on the people it should have protected. He could have passed the problem to the next generation. He chose to confront it,” she said. While acknowledging the economic hardship triggered by the reforms, Sulaiman-Ibrahim said the government recognised the sacrifices Nigerian households had made. She, however, maintained that the measures were beginning to produce positive outcomes, citing improvements in external reserves, easing inflationary pressures and renewed investor confidence. The minister said the government did not take the difficulties experienced by citizens lightly, adding that the sacrifices would ultimately prove worthwhile as the results of the reforms became more evident. “Those decisions came at a cost and Nigerian families have felt it. No one in this government takes that sacrifice lightly, least of all Mr. President. But I say to you today, with conviction, that the sacrifice is not in vain. The results are beginning to show,” she stated. She identified the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), the new tax laws and financial autonomy for local governments as key policies intended to ensure that the gains from the economic reforms reach ordinary Nigerians. According to her, the student loan scheme is widening access to higher education for students from disadvantaged backgrounds, while the tax reforms are intended to shield low-income earners and small businesses from excessive taxation. “Under the new tax laws, low-income earners and small businesses are protected, so that those with the least are asked to carry the least. And with financial autonomy for local governments, resources now flow closer to our communities,” she said. Addressing the implications of the reforms for women and vulnerable households, the minister said the administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda had placed social protection and the creation of economic opportunities for women and girls among its priorities. She explained that her evaluation of government policies was based on their practical impact on women engaged in trading, girls attending school and families living on the margins of society. She added that the administration remained committed to tackling the difficulties confronting vulnerable Nigerians. “I judge every reform by one test. Does it reach the woman in the market, the girl in the classroom and the family at the margins? On that test, I can say with pride that our leader and father has kept women at the heart of the Renewed Hope Agenda,” the minister said. On questions concerning the tangible benefits of the reforms and Nigeria’s increasing borrowing needs, Sulaiman-Ibrahim argued that countries required substantial investments in productive sectors and essential infrastructure to achieve sustainable economic growth. She maintained that public borrowing was not necessarily a sign of economic failure, noting that developed economies also relied on debt to finance their activities. She cited the United States as an example of a country that continued to borrow despite having one of the world’s largest economies. “Show me a country that has developed, that has a strong economy, that is not in debt. I think the most indebted country in the world is the United States of America. And they’re still borrowing,” she said. The minister further stressed that borrowing should be assessed against the economic value and developmental benefits of the projects financed with the funds. She acknowledged the importance of responsible debt management, insisting that borrowed resources must be directed towards projects and sectors capable of generating measurable economic returns. According to her, Nigeria still has significant investment gaps in critical infrastructure and essential systems, making additional resources necessary to address longstanding development challenges. “One thing I can assure you of is Mr. President will take us to the promised land. He means well for the Nigerian people,” she added. On the reported increase in the number of out-of-school children in Nigeria from 14 million to 20 million, Sulaiman-Ibrahim acknowledged the seriousness of the challenge but said the government was adopting broader interventions beyond conventional classroom education. She identified science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education, alongside technical and vocational education and training (TVET), as part of the measures being pursued to expand learning opportunities and equip young people with relevant skills. The minister also said the administration had increased its attention to early childhood education, skills acquisition and investment in the education sector. She explained that the government was adopting a coordinated, whole-of-government approach to address educational challenges and improve children’s access to learning. “Mr. President is a thinking President, so we’re running a thinking government. We’re very deliberate,” she said. Sulaiman-Ibrahim further urged Nigerians to understand that the benefits of government reforms and policy announcements might not be felt immediately, explaining that implementation often depended on funding arrangements, administrative adjustments and coordination among relevant institutions. She expressed confidence that the Tinubu administration would fulfil its commitments, while calling on the media to provide citizens with accurate and factual information about the reforms as political activities intensify ahead of the 2027 general elections. The minister urged journalists to ensure that public discussions about the administration’s policies were guided by verifiable information rather than misinformation as the country approaches the next general election. “As 2027 approaches, the national debate will grow louder. Let it also grow wiser, and let it rest on facts. I urge you, the press, to carry those facts to every corner of this country,” she said. The forthcoming book unveiling is expected to feature President Tinubu as the Special Guest of Honour, with Alhaji Aliko Dangote serving as Chief Launcher and Alhaji Abdul Samad Rabiu as Co-Chief Launcher. High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, is listed as the Chief Host, while the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, will serve as Host. The Senate President, Speaker of the House of Representatives, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, state governors and other prominent political and business leaders are also expected to attend the event. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/m.title_zh: 部长称：蒂努布的改革正在取得成效，预计将取得更多成果
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/m.body_zh: 妇女事务和社会发展部长哈吉娅·伊曼·苏莱曼·易卜拉欣为总统博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布的经济改革辩护，称尽管尼日利亚人面临经济困难，这些必要而大胆的决定已经开始取得成果。苏莱曼-易卜拉欣周二在一场全国性新闻发布会上作出上述表示。此次发布会是为推介一本探讨蒂努布改革议程的新书而举行的。她说，总统选择应对国家长期存在的经济问题，而不是把负担转嫁给后代。这本书名为《改革的勇气：博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统，GCFR——跨越2027年：治国术、国家复兴愿景》，由PBAT入户推广运动推动，旨在展示本届政府过去三年的政策和成就。部长表示，蒂努布于2023年5月29日在经济形势严峻的情况下就任，这些形势要求采取果断行动，解决尼日利亚经济、收入征管体系和公共财政方面的结构性弱点。她解释道，汽油补贴正在消耗本可用于教育、医疗和道路基础设施等基本公共服务的资金。她还批评现行税制给本应受到保护的人施加了不成比例的负担。苏莱曼-易卜拉欣说：“总统先生于2023年5月29日宣誓就职时，接手的是不能再拖延的艰难选择。汽油补贴正在耗尽本应用于学校、医院和道路的资源，而我们的税制把最沉重的负担压在最应受到保护的人身上。他本可以把问题留给下一代，但他选择直面问题。”苏莱曼-易卜拉欣承认改革引发了经济困境，但表示政府认识到尼日利亚家庭为此作出的牺牲。不过，她坚持认为，这些措施已开始产生积极成效，并列举了外汇储备增加、通胀压力缓解以及投资者信心恢复等变化。部长说，政府没有轻视公民所经历的困难，并补充称，随着改革成效日益明显，这些牺牲最终将证明是值得的。她表示：“这些决定是有代价的，尼日利亚家庭已经切身感受到了。政府没有一个人会轻视这种牺牲，总统先生更是如此。但我今天要坚定地告诉你们，这些牺牲不会白费，成果已经开始显现。”她把尼日利亚教育贷款基金（NELFUND）、新税法以及赋予地方政府财政自主权列为确保经济改革成果惠及普通尼日利亚人的关键政策。据她介绍，学生贷款计划正在为来自弱势家庭的学生拓宽接受高等教育的机会，而税收改革的目的是保护低收入者和小型企业免受过度征税。她表示：“根据新税法，低收入者和小型企业得到保护，使负担最少的人承担最少的负担。随着地方政府获得财政自主权，资源现在能够更贴近我们的社区流向。”在谈及改革对妇女和弱势家庭的影响时，部长表示，本届政府的“更新希望议程”把社会保护以及为妇女和女孩创造经济机会列为优先事项。她解释说，自己对政府政策的评价依据是这些政策对从事贸易的妇女、上学的女孩以及生活在美国社会边缘的家庭所产生的实际影响。她补充称，本届政府仍致力于解决弱势尼日利亚人面临的困难。部长说：“我用一个标准衡量每一项改革：它是否惠及市场里的妇女、课堂上的女孩和社会边缘的家庭？按照这个标准，我可以自豪地说，我们的领袖和父亲始终把妇女置于‘更新希望议程’的核心。”在谈及改革带来的切实好处以及尼日利亚不断上升的借款需求时，苏莱曼-易卜拉欣认为，国家要实现可持续经济增长，就必须对生产性部门和基本基础设施进行大量投资。她坚持认为，公共借款未必是经济失败的标志，并指出发达经济体同样依靠债务为自身活动提供资金。她以美国为例，指出美国尽管拥有世界上最大的经济体之一，仍在持续借款。她说：“请给我举出一个已经发展、经济强劲却没有债务的国家。我认为，世界上负债最多的国家是美利坚合众国，而且他们仍在继续借款。”部长进一步强调，评价借款时，应结合这些资金所支持项目的经济价值和开发效益。她承认负责任的债务管理十分重要，同时坚持借入的资源必须用于能够产生可衡量经济回报的项目和部门。据她介绍，尼日利亚在关键基础设施和基本系统方面仍存在巨大投资缺口，因此需要额外资源来解决长期存在的发展挑战。她补充道：“我可以向你保证的一件事是，总统先生会带领我们抵达应许之地。他真心希望尼日利亚人民过得更好。”在谈及尼日利亚失学儿童人数据报从1400万增至2000万的问题时，苏莱曼-易卜拉欣承认这一挑战十分严峻，但表示政府正在采取超越传统课堂教育的综合干预措施。她把科学、技术、工程和数学（STEM）教育以及技术与职业教育培训（TVET）列为正在推进的措施，以扩大学习机会并为年轻人提供相关技能。部长还表示，本届政府加强了对幼儿教育、技能培养和教育领域投资的关注。她解释道，政府正采取协调一致、全政府参与的方式解决教育难题，改善儿童获得学习机会的条件。她说：“总统先生是一位善于思考的总统，所以我们正在建设一个善于思考的政府。我们的每一项行动都经过深思熟虑。”苏莱曼-易卜拉欣进一步敦促尼日利亚人理解，政府改革和政策公告带来的益处可能不会立即显现，因为落实工作往往取决于资金安排、行政调整以及相关机构之间的协调。她对蒂努布政府将履行承诺表示信心，同时呼吁媒体在2027年大选前政治活动日益激烈之际，向公民提供有关改革的准确、真实信息。部长敦促 journalists 确保公众对政府政策的讨论以可核实的信息而非错误信息为依据，并让这些事实伴随全国性辩论日益高涨。她说：“随着2027年临近，全国性辩论会越来越激烈。也要让它变得更加明智，让它建立在事实之上。我敦促你们新闻界把这些事实传遍这个国家的每个角落。”即将举行的新书发布会预计邀请蒂努布总统担任荣誉嘉宾，由Alhaji Aliko Dangote担任首席启动人，Alhaji Abdul Samad Rabiu担任联合首席启动人。 popularly known as Tompolo 的 High Chief Government Ekpemupolo将担任首席主持，联邦首都 Territory 部长Nyesom Wike将担任主持人。参议院议长、众议院议长、联邦政府秘书、州长以及其他政界和商界领袖也预计出席活动。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/s.summary: He urged the relevant authorities to strengthen security operations and establish a sustained presence in vulnerable communities to prevent armed groups from exploiting gaps in surveillance along the boundaries of the three states. “The primary purpose of governance is to protect the lives and property of the people,” Monguno said, commending Lau for bringing the plight of his constituents to the attention of the Senate.

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/s.body: • Lawmakers demand more personnel for Taraba, Plateau, Bauchi border communities •NEMA, North-East Development Commission urged to provide emergency relief The Senate has called for the immediate deployment of additional security personnel and the establishment of security camps along the borders of Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi states following the killing of about 80 people by armed bandits in Binari community, Karim-Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State. The upper chamber also urged the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and the North-East Development Commission (NEDC) to provide urgent relief materials to residents affected by the attack. The resolutions followed a motion raised during plenary by Senator Isa Lau, who drew attention to the persistent attacks on rural communities in his constituency and the growing threat to lives and property. Lau said the latest assault had claimed scores of lives, heightened insecurity and forced residents to flee their homes, warning that urgent intervention was necessary to prevent further killings. He lamented the continued attacks by armed bandits on rural communities, stressing that the government must fulfil its constitutional responsibility to protect lives and property. The senator warned that failure to take decisive action could lead to further loss of lives, the destruction of communities and a worsening humanitarian crisis in the affected areas. He urged the relevant authorities to strengthen security operations and establish a sustained presence in vulnerable communities to prevent armed groups from exploiting gaps in surveillance along the boundaries of the three states. Contributing to the debate, Senator Mohammed Monguno described the motion as timely, stressing that protecting lives and property remained the fundamental responsibility of government. “The primary purpose of governance is to protect the lives and property of the people,” Monguno said, commending Lau for bringing the plight of his constituents to the attention of the Senate. Following deliberations on the motion, the Senate called on security agencies to deploy additional personnel to the affected communities and establish more security camps along the Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi borders. The proposed measures are aimed at strengthening surveillance, improving security coverage in the vulnerable areas and preventing further attacks on rural settlements. The Senate also urged NEMA and the NEDC to provide emergency assistance to displaced residents and other victims of the violence. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/h.body: The House of Representatives has approved a N100.5 billion promissory note programme to reimburse the Yobe State Government for the construction of the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu, following the federal government’s decision to take over the facility. The approved sum of N100,509,017,234.55 was granted on Wednesday after the House considered a report submitted by its Committee on Aids, Loans and Debt Management. Speaking with journalists at the National Assembly in Abuja, the committee’s chairman, Abubakar Hassan Nalaraba, said members conducted due diligence and carried out an inspection of the airport before recommending the reimbursement. He explained that officials of the Federal Ministries of Aviation and Finance as well as other relevant government agencies, provided technical assessments and supporting documents for the project. Nalaraba said the committee approved the reimbursement after reviewing the findings of its oversight exercise and receiving technical reports from the Ministries of Aviation and Finance, alongside relevant accounting authorities. According to him, the committee was satisfied with the quality of the airport’s infrastructure and equipment, adding that professionals who assessed the facilities certified them as meeting the required standards. The committee’s report disclosed that the Federal Ministry of Aviation had inspected the completed airport and confirmed that the quality of construction complied with the standards required for the federal government to assume ownership of the facility. It further established that the Yobe State Government had settled payments due to the contractors responsible for executing the project, while the Bureau of Public Procurement confirmed that the procurement process complied with the relevant requirements. In arriving at its recommendation, the committee examined documents and submissions from the Yobe State Government, the Federal Ministries of Finance and Aviation, the Federal Executive Council and the Bureau of Public Procurement. The documents reviewed included contract agreements, certificates of completion, evidence of payments to contractors, due-process compliance reviews and the Bureau of Public Procurement’s certificate of no objection. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had earlier sought the National Assembly’s approval for the promissory note programme in a communication read on the floor of the House on October 13, 2026. The request was made in accordance with the Debt Management Office (Establishment) Act, 2003, and the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007, which require legislative approval for the programme. Promissory note programmes are instruments used by the federal government to settle outstanding verified liabilities, including reimbursements to state governments that execute projects on behalf of the federal authorities. Speaking on the potential economic benefits of the airport, Nalaraba said the facility would provide additional value to the people of Yobe State and help attract investments to the state and the country. He noted that the construction of critical infrastructure in a state could improve the welfare of residents while creating opportunities for economic growth and investment. Also speaking, a member of the committee representing Yobe State, Mohammed Jajere, said the airport had the potential to become a major cargo hub for the North-East, particularly for the transportation of agricultural produce and raw materials. Jajere described Yobe as an agrarian state with abundant agricultural products and raw materials, expressing optimism that the cargo airport would provide an important transportation link for the region. He added that the facility could facilitate the movement of agricultural produce from the North-East to other markets, thereby improving access to buyers and supporting economic activities across the region. However, journalists questioned the commercial viability of airports in Nigeria, citing a report attributed to the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) which indicated that only three of the country’s 22 domestic and international airports were commercially viable. In response, Nalaraba said the committee based its recommendation on the technical assessments conducted by the relevant aviation authorities, noting that lawmakers relied on the expertise of professionals to evaluate the operational prospects of the facility. He maintained that officials of the Ministry of Aviation and FAAN had inspected the airport and certified it as viable and ready for commercial operations. The committee chairman further stressed that the project had undergone the necessary administrative and technical assessments before the reimbursement request was presented to the National Assembly for consideration. Nalaraba also clarified that the approved amount was not new funding for the construction of the airport but a reimbursement to the Yobe State Government for expenditure already incurred on a project the federal government had decided to take over. He explained that the money had already been spent on the construction of the international cargo airport, describing the proposed payment as a repayment to the state rather than fresh funding for the project. The committee chairman added that Yobe State had undertaken the construction despite aviation being a matter within the exclusive legislative jurisdiction of the federal government. Addressing concerns about the possibility of additional financial obligations arising from the project, the committee indicated the federal government’s takeover would transfer responsibility for the airport, including its future maintenance and development, to the federal authorities. The committee also indicated that the reimbursement would be made as a one-off payment, although details of the specific payment arrangements were not fully disclosed during the briefing. With the approval, attention is expected to shift to the federal government’s management of the airport and its capacity to attract sufficient commercial activity to justify the public investment, particularly through the transportation of agricultural produce and other cargo from the North-East. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/h.title_zh: 众议院批准为博贝机场拨款1005亿奈拉
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/h.body_zh: 众议院已批准一项价值1005亿奈拉的期票计划，用于偿还约贝州政府为在达马图鲁建设穆罕马杜·布哈里国际机场而支出的费用，此前联邦政府已决定接管该机场。众议院审议其援助、贷款和债务管理委员会提交的报告后，于周三批准拨款100,509,017,234.55奈拉。委员会主席阿布巴卡尔·哈桑·纳拉拉巴在阿布贾国民议会向记者表示，委员会成员进行了尽职调查，并实地检查了机场，之后才建议偿还相关款项。他解释说，联邦航空部、财政部以及其他相关政府机构的官员为该项目提供了技术评估和支持文件。纳拉拉巴说，委员会在审查监督工作的调查结果，并收到航空部、财政部及相关会计机构的技术报告后，批准了偿还方案。据他介绍，委员会对机场基础设施和设备的质量表示满意，并称对这些设施进行评估的专业人士证明其符合规定标准。委员会的报告披露，联邦航空部已对建成的机场进行检查，并确认其建设质量符合联邦政府接管该设施所需的标准。报告还确认，约贝州政府已经向负责实施项目的承包商支付了应付款项，公共采购局也确认采购流程符合相关要求。委员会在提出建议时，审查了约贝州政府、联邦财政部、联邦航空部、联邦执行委员会和公共采购局提交的文件及材料。审查的文件包括合同协议、竣工证明、向承包商付款的凭证、法定程序合规审查结果，以及公共采购局出具的无异议证明。博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统此前曾请求国民议会批准这项期票计划，相关函件于2026年10月13日在众议院全体会议上宣读。该请求依据《2003年债务管理办公室（设立）法》和《2007年财政责任法》提出，这两部法律要求该计划必须获得立法批准。期票计划是联邦政府用于清偿经核实未付债务的工具，其中包括向代联邦机构实施项目的州政府偿还费用。谈及机场可能带来的经济效益，纳拉拉巴表示，该设施将为约贝州民众创造更多价值，并有助于吸引对该州和整个国家的投资。他指出，在一个州建设关键基础设施可以改善居民福祉，同时为经济增长和投资创造机会。委员会中代表约贝州的成员穆罕默德·贾杰雷也表示，该机场有望成为东北部地区的重要货运枢纽，尤其适合运输农产品和原材料。贾杰雷称约贝州是一个农产品和原材料丰富的小农州，并乐观认为这座货运机场将为该地区提供重要的运输联系。他补充说，该设施可以促进东北部农产品运往其他市场，从而改善买家获取货物的便利性，并推动全地区的经济活动。然而，记者质疑尼日利亚机场的商业可行性，并援引一份据称出自尼日利亚联邦机场管理局（FAAN）的报告，称该国22座国内和国际机场中只有3座具有商业可行性。对此，纳拉拉巴表示，委员会的建议以相关航空主管部门开展的技术评估为依据，议员依赖专业人士的专业知识评估该设施的运营前景。他坚称，航空部和FAAN的官员已经检查了机场，并确认其具备商业运营条件且已准备就绪。委员会主席进一步强调，在将偿还请求提交国民议会审议之前，该项目已经完成必要的行政和技术评估。纳拉拉巴还澄清，批准的金额并非用于机场建设的新资金，而是联邦政府决定接管该项目后，偿还约贝州政府已经发生的支出。他解释说，这笔钱已经用于建设这座国际机场，因此拟议付款是对该州已经支付费用的补偿，而不是为该项目提供新资金。委员会主席还表示，尽管航空事务属于联邦政府专属立法管辖范围，约贝州仍承担了机场建设。针对该项目可能产生额外财政负担的担忧，委员会指出，联邦政府接管后将把机场的责任，包括未来的维护和发展，交由联邦主管部门承担。委员会还表示，偿还款项将一次性支付，不过简报会并未完全披露具体支付安排的细节。随着批准落地，公众预计将关注联邦政府如何管理这座机场，以及其能否吸引足够的商业活动来证明公共投资的合理性，尤其是通过运输东北部农产品和其他货物。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办事处。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，覆盖所有平台，服务于政治、商业、专业和外交精英及更广泛的中产阶层，同时为有抱负者和千禧一代提供新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。这份报纸是一项公共信任，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育和社区等议题，呈现人与社会的交汇之处。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

Gen. General Theophilus Yakubu Danjuma(Rtd). The House, while adopting a motion jointly sponsored by three lawmakers – Hons Jonathan Gaza Gbefwi, Mark Useni and Ayuba Zaku Dampar, said the university should now be known as T. Y. Danjuma Federal University, Wukari (TYDFUW), subject to the necessary amendment of its enabling Act. The Green Chamber also mandated its Committee on University Education to engage relevant stakeholders and facilitate the legislative measures required to give effect to the proposed renaming. The motion was titled: ‘Call to Rename Federal University, Wukari, Taraba State, as T. Y. Danjuma Federal University, Wukari. Moving the motion on behalf of his colleagues, Hon. Gaza noted that Federal University, Wukari, Taraba State, was established in 2011 to expand access to higher education and promote research and national development. Gaza argued that the contributions of Lieutenant General Danjuma (Rtd), to Nigeria through military and public service, philanthropy and support for education, healthcare, and vulnerable communities deserved such recognition. He noted that naming the university after the former Chief of Army Staff would honour his contributions to national development and preserve a legacy of service for future generations. The motion was seconded by Hon. Bamidele Salam. When the motion was put to a voice vote, the lawmakers overwhelmingly voted in its favour. Speaker Abbas Tajudeen, who presided over plenary, commended Hon. Gaza for bringing the motion, saying, “Hon. Jonathan, thank you for remembering our leader, our mentor. Your motion is apt. The federal government will do the needful. God bless you.” The motion was consequently referred to the House Committee on University Education for further legislative action. We’ve got the edge. 詹姆斯·昆，7秒前发布于新闻

众议院敦促联邦政府将塔拉巴州武卡里联邦大学以资深政治家、前国防部长、退役中将西奥菲卢斯·雅库布·丹朱马阁下之名重新命名。

众议院通过了一项由3名议员——乔纳森·加扎·格贝夫维、马克·乌塞尼和阿尤巴·扎库·丹帕尔——联合提出的动议。动议称，在对相关授权法案作出必要修订后，该大学应更名为T. Y. Danjuma Federal University, Wukari（TYDFUW，武卡里T. Y. 丹朱马联邦大学）。

众议院还授权其大学教育委员会与相关利益攸关方接洽，并推动落实拟议更名所需的立法措施。

该动议的标题为：“呼吁将塔拉巴州武卡里联邦大学更名为武卡里T. Y. 丹朱马联邦大学。”

加扎议员代表同僚提出动议时指出，塔拉巴州武卡里联邦大学成立于2011年，旨在扩大高等教育覆盖面，并推动研究和国家发展。加扎认为，丹朱马中将以退役身份通过军旅和公共服务、慈善事业以及对口教育、医疗和弱势群体的支持为尼日利亚作出的贡献，值得获得这种认可。他指出，以这位前陆军参谋长命名该大学，既能表彰他对国家发展的贡献，也能为后代留下服务国家的精神传承。

该动议由巴米德莱·萨拉姆议员附议。

动议付诸唱名表决时，议员们以压倒性多数表示赞成。主持全体会议的众议院议长阿巴斯·塔朱丁称赞加扎议员提出该动议，并表示：“乔纳森议员，感谢您记得我们的领袖、我们的导师。您的动议十分恰当。联邦政府将采取必要行动。愿上帝保佑您。”

随后，该动议被提交众议院大学教育委员会进一步采取立法行动。

https://leadership.ng/state-police-bill-.summary: The bill is the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, transmitted by the National Assembly to the 36 state Houses of Assembly for concurrence. Presenting the bill, Abdullahi said it seeks to amend the 1999 Constitution to establish state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force as the federal police.
https://leadership.ng/state-police-bill-.summary_zh: 该法案是《尼日利亚联邦共和国宪法（第六次修订）法案（2026年）》，由国民议会提交给36个州议会审议并表示同意。在提交法案时，Abdullahi表示，该法案旨在修订1999年宪法，以建立各州警察机构，同时保留尼日利亚警察部队作为联邦警察机构。
https://leadership.ng/state-police-bill-.body: The bill was passed on Tuesday evening during plenary presided over by the Speaker, Alhaji Tukur Bala Bodinga. Bodinga, who confirmed the development to LEADERSHIP, said the House would soon issue an official statement on its decision. “Yes, we have passed the bill yesterday. You will see the statement any moment from now,” he said. The bill is the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, transmitted by the National Assembly to the 36 state Houses of Assembly for concurrence. The motion was moved by the Deputy Majority Leader, Mustapha Abdullahi (APC – Sokoto South II). Presenting the bill, Abdullahi said it seeks to amend the 1999 Constitution to establish state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force as the federal police. He said the bill was transmitted by the executive, considered by the Senate on June 24 and the House of Representatives on July 23, and presented to the Sokoto Assembly on September 22. Abdullahi explained that under the proposed framework, the federal police would handle interstate and international crimes, terrorism, cybercrime, border security, policing of the Federal Capital Territory and protection of federal assets. He said state police services would be responsible for law enforcement, maintenance of public order and safety, protection of lives and property and investigation of local crimes. He added that the head of a state police service would be known as the State Commander of Police, to be appointed by the governor on the recommendation of the National Police Council, subject to confirmation by the State House of Assembly. He said a State Police Service Commission would be responsible for appointment, promotion and discipline of personnel and would receive funds directly from the state’s Consolidated Revenue Fund to ensure financial autonomy. The passage brings the number of state assemblies that have endorsed the bill to 28, exceeding the constitutional requirement of 24 states, or two-thirds of the 36 assemblies, needed for alteration of the Constitution. The development comes amid persistent security challenges in Sokoto and the North-West, where banditry, kidnapping and attacks on rural communities have disrupted farming and livelihoods. Proponents argue that officers recruited from local communities would better understand the terrain and improve intelligence gathering. The latest approvals were recorded in Kano, Sokoto, Ebonyi and Lagos on Tuesday, according to reports. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/state-police-bill-.title_zh: 州警察法案：索科托州议会加入另外27个议会行列
https://leadership.ng/state-police-bill-.body_zh: 该法案于周二晚间在众议院议长Alhaji Tukur Bala Bodinga主持的全会上获得通过。Bodinga向《LEADERSHIP》证实了这一进展，并表示众议院很快将就其决定发布正式声明。他说：“是的，我们昨天通过了该法案。你们很快就会看到声明。”该法案是《1999年尼日利亚联邦共和国宪法（第六次修订）法案（2026年）》，由国民议会提交给36个州议会审议并取得一致同意。动议由多数党副领袖Mustapha Abdullahi（APC–索科托南二选区）提出。Abdullahi在提交法案时表示，该法案旨在修订1999年宪法，以建立各州警察机构，同时保留尼日利亚警察部队作为联邦警察。他说，该法案由行政部门提交，参议院于6月24日审议，众议院于7月23日审议，并于9月22日提交索科托州议会。Abdullahi解释称，根据拟议框架，联邦警察将负责处理跨州和国际犯罪、恐怖主义、网络犯罪、边境安全、联邦首都辖区治安以及联邦资产保护。他说，各州警察机构将负责执法、维护公共秩序与安全、保护生命和财产，以及调查地方犯罪。他补充说，各州警察机构的负责人将称为警察州指挥官，由州长根据国家警察委员会的建议任命，并须经州议会确认。他说，州警察服务委员会将负责人员的任命、晋升和纪律管理，并直接从州综合收入基金获得资金，以确保财政自主。该法案获通过后，已有28个州议会表示支持，超过修改宪法所需的24个州、即36个州议会中三分之二的要求。索科托州及西北部持续面临安全挑战，土匪活动、绑架和对农村社区的袭击已扰乱农业生产和生计。支持者认为，从当地社区招募的警员能够更好地了解地形，并改善情报收集工作。据报道，周二最新获得批准的是卡诺、索科托、埃博尼和拉各斯州。欢迎关注我们的优势服务。实时报道、突发独家消息和独家视角将直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入《LEADERSHIP NEWS》的WhatsApp频道，获取全天候最新动态 →

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alak.title: Alake denies $700bn minerals sale, inaugurates Nigeria-US committee
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alak.summary: ABUJA — Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, has dismissed reports that Nigeria sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to the United States, insisting that no national asset has been sold or transferred under the bilateral cooperation framework.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alak.summary_zh: 阿布贾——固体矿产发展部长Dele Alake博士否认了有关尼日利亚向美国出售价值$700 billion固体矿产的报道，坚持称在双边合作框架下没有出售或转让任何国有资产。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alak.body: ABUJA — Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, has dismissed reports that Nigeria sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to the United States, insisting that no national asset has been sold or transferred under the bilateral cooperation framework. Alake spoke on Tuesday in Abuja while inaugurating the Nigeria-United States Committee on Strategic Cooperation in the Solid Minerals Sector, describing the reports as false and clarifying that the agreement was designed to attract investment and promote partnerships between American investors and Nigerian operators. “There is no sale of any Nigerian asset. There’s nothing exchanging hands,” he said. The minister explained that the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed by Nigeria and the US was a government-to-government platform intended to facilitate business-to-business engagements, rather than transfer ownership of Nigeria’s mineral resources to foreign interests. “We created a platform to facilitate mingling of US investment ventures with Nigeria’s local operators. It is in the public domain. We signed it in public and published it in four or five national newspapers,” he said. The committee’s inauguration followed the strategic cooperation framework established between both countries during the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York. Alake also dismissed claims that the United States intended to take over Nigeria’s mineral resources and security architecture, describing the reports as misleading. He said the partnership aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s economic diversification agenda, which seeks to reduce the country’s dependence on crude oil through the sustainable development of its mineral resources. According to him, Nigeria is seeking to change the pattern of international economic transactions in which resource-rich African countries export raw materials without retaining sufficient value from their exploitation. “We have the resources, the critical elements the world needs to transit to clean energy. So we are creating a new paradigm — you bring your capital, expertise and technology, to match with our natural resources and create a win-win situation. The investor gains, Nigeria gains,” he said. The minister lamented that Nigeria had historically operated a mono-product economy, while much of its solid minerals sector remained informal, with ores transported “from pit to port” without adequate local processing. He said the Federal Government had introduced a policy making local processing a condition for the granting of mineral titles, adding that investors must demonstrate a clear pathway for processing minerals within the country. According to Alake, the policy has encouraged the establishment of processing facilities across the country, including what he described as West Africa’s largest lithium processing plant, recently commissioned in Nasarawa State by the Vice President. He said the government’s reform efforts also informed the establishment of the African Minerals Strategy Group, which aims to strengthen cooperation among African countries on mineral development. Alake attributed renewed investor confidence to the macroeconomic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration, which he said provided assurances on security of tenure and the repatriation of profits. Charging members of the newly inaugurated committee to discharge their responsibilities diligently, the minister described their assignment as critical to achieving the President’s $1 trillion economy target. He urged the committee to coordinate activities, identify viable investment opportunities and translate the Nigeria-US cooperation framework into measurable outcomes that would strengthen the country’s position in the global solid minerals industry. In his welcome address, the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development, Engr Faruk Yusuf Yabo, said the inauguration would translate growing bilateral engagements into a structured framework for practical cooperation and investment mobilisation. Also speaking, Economic Officer at the US Embassy, Jonathan Baas, said US President Donald Trump had prioritised three areas for American embassies: energy, artificial intelligence and superintelligence, as well as critical minerals. Baas said Washington was seeking partnerships that would secure critical mineral supply chains while ensuring that partner countries benefited from the value generated. “We just signed a contract today on looking into building AI data centres in Nigeria at the Nigerian Economic Summit. That’s the direction Washington wants us to go,” he said. In his vote of thanks, the Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of the Nigeria Solid Minerals Company (NSMC) said the committee would coordinate implementation, facilitate investment and monitor progress towards achieving the objectives of the Nigeria-US cooperation framework. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alak.title_zh: 阿拉基否认出售7,000亿美元矿产，并为尼日利亚—美国委员会揭幕
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alak.body_zh:
阿布贾——固体矿产开发部长德勒·阿拉基博士驳斥了尼日利亚向美国出售价值7000亿美元固体矿产的报道，坚称尼日利亚与美国双边合作框架下没有出售或转让任何国家资产。阿拉基周二在阿布贾为尼日利亚—美国固体矿产领域战略合作委员会揭幕时发表上述言论。他称这些报道是虚假消息，并澄清协议旨在吸引投资，促进美国投资者与尼日利亚运营商开展合作。他说：“没有任何尼日利亚资产被出售，也没有任何东西易手。”

部长解释道，尼日利亚与美国签署的谅解备忘录是一个政府间平台，旨在促进企业间商业接洽，而非将尼日利亚矿产资源的所有权转让给外国利益集团。他说：“我们搭建了一个平台，让美国投资业务与尼日利亚本地运营商携手合作。协议已向公众公开，我们公开签署，并刊登在四五家全国性报纸上。”

该委员会的揭幕仪式是在两国于纽约举行的第81届联合国大会期间确立战略合作框架后举行的。阿拉基还驳斥了美国意图接管尼日利亚矿产资源和安全架构的说法，称这些报道具有误导性。他说，合作符合博拉·蒂努布总统的经济多元化议程，即通过可持续开发矿产资源，减少尼日利亚对原油的依赖。

据他介绍，尼日利亚正寻求改变国际经济交易模式。在这一模式下，非洲资源丰富国家出口原材料，却未能从资源开发中保留足够的价值。他说：“我们拥有资源，也拥有世界转向清洁能源所需的关键元素。因此，我们正在创立一种新范式——你们带来资本、专业知识和技术，与我们的自然资源相结合，创造双赢局面。投资者获得收益，尼日利亚也获得收益。”

部长惋惜地表示，尼日利亚长期以来实行单一产品经济模式，而其固体矿产行业很大程度上仍处于非正规状态，矿石通常“从矿坑运往港口”，缺乏充分的本地加工。他说，联邦政府出台了一项政策，将本地加工设为授予矿业权的前提条件，投资者必须证明其在国内加工矿产的明确路径。据阿拉基称，这项政策鼓励了全国范围内加工设施的建设，其中包括他所说的西非最大锂加工厂，该厂最近已由副总统在纳萨拉瓦州主持投产。

他说，政府的改革努力也为非洲矿产战略小组的成立提供了指导，该小组旨在加强非洲各国在矿产开发方面的合作。阿拉基将投资者信心回升归因于蒂努布政府实施的宏观经济改革，并称这些改革就土地使用权的保障以及利润汇回提供了保证。

部长要求新揭幕的委员会成员勤勉履职，并表示委员会肩负的使命对于实现总统提出的经济规模达到1万亿美元的目标至关重要。他敦促委员会协调各项活动、发掘可行的投资机会，并将尼日利亚—美国合作框架转化为可衡量的成果，从而巩固尼日利亚在全球固体矿产产业中的地位。

在欢迎辞中，固体矿产开发部常务秘书法鲁克·优素福·亚博工程师表示，此次揭幕将把日益增多的双边接触转化为务实合作和投资动员的结构化框架。美国大使馆经济官员乔纳森·巴斯也出席并发言，称美国总统唐纳德·特朗普已要求美国大使馆优先关注三个领域：能源、人工智能与超级智能，以及关键矿产。巴斯说，华盛顿正在寻求能够保障关键矿产供应链的合作伙伴关系，同时确保伙伴国家能够分享所创造的价值。

他说：“我们今天刚在尼日利亚经济峰会上签署了一份合同，研究在尼日利亚建设人工智能数据中心的可行性。这就是华盛顿希望我们前进的方向。”

尼日利亚固体矿产公司首席执行官兼董事总经理在致谢辞中表示，该委员会将协调合作框架的落实，促进投资，并监督实现尼日利亚—美国合作框架目标的进展。

本文所发表的意见不代表Vanguard Newspapers及其任何员工的观点

https://www.myjoyonline.com/telecel-ghan.body: Telecel Ghana marked World Sustainability Day with a renewed commitment to practical climate action, showcasing how it integrates sustainability into its network operations, products, employee culture, and social impact initiatives. The organisation celebrated this year’s World Sustainability Day as a premium partner of the Ghana National Climate & ESG Policy Summit 2026, organised by Intelligence Nature International under the auspices of the Office of the Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability. The summit brought together policymakers, regulators, development institutions, and private-sector leaders to discuss Ghana’s green transition and businesses' role in accelerating climate action. Speaking during a private-sector panel discussion, Rita Agyeiwaa Rockson, Head of Sustainability, Foundation and External Communications at Telecel Ghana, called for sustainability to move from complex concepts and high-level commitments to practical actions organisations, entrepreneurs, and individuals can understand and adopt. “Sustainability cannot remain a conversation that only happens at the top, based on the assumption that everyone understands it. We need to simplify the language and connect it to the everyday decisions of organisations and individuals. When people understand how sustainability reduces costs, strengthens resilience and improves access to customers and investors, it becomes relevant to them,” Rita said. She encouraged organisations to start with achievable interventions, measure results, and use credible data to build toward broader climate ambitions. “There are practical actions that corporate organisations, small businesses and individuals can take to contribute to the larger sustainability goals we want to achieve. The important thing is to start, collect the data and communicate the impact being created,” she added. For Telecel Ghana, this approach is reflected in how the organisation integrates sustainability across its operations. To reduce the environmental footprint of its operations, Telecel Ghana is transitioning parts of its network infrastructure to renewable energy, with 15 exchanges currently powered by solar. The investment reduces its reliance on the national grid and supports more sustainable network operations. In August 2026, Telecel Ghana introduced its biodegradable Eco-SIM, manufactured with 90 per cent less plastic than standard SIM cards. The organisation has also planted more than 40,000 trees across the Achimota, Chipa and South Fomangso forest reserves, contributing to reforestation and ecosystem restoration. Its sustainability efforts also extend to digital and financial inclusion. Telecel Ghana’s services let customers complete essential transactions remotely, reducing the need to travel, costs, and associated emissions. Its digital inclusion initiatives equip entrepreneurs, including women-led businesses, with the skills and tools to improve efficiency, access new markets and strengthen their enterprises. According to Rita, inclusion must remain central to Ghana’s transition to a greener economy. “As we build the communities and economies of the future, we must pay attention to who is being included. Digital and financial inclusion are essential to ensuring that the benefits of sustainable development reach entrepreneurs, small businesses and underserved communities,” she said. Throughout the Month, Telecel Ghana also encouraged employees to make more environmentally responsible choices. Activities included No-Plastic Days, which promoted alternatives to single-use plastics, and a Green Market that connected employees with local entrepreneurs offering environmentally responsible and locally made products. The activities demonstrated how everyday choices can promote responsible consumption while creating opportunities for entrepreneurs advancing circular production. The organization’s participation in the summit extended the internal campaign into a broader national conversation on climate action, sustainable finance, ESG disclosure, carbon markets and green investment. “We recognise that sustainability is a journey and that there is still more work to be done. Our ambition is clear: connect people and organisations in ways that support a more inclusive society while progressively reducing our environmental impact. Achieving this requires collaboration across sectors, practical action and consistent measurement of progress,” Rita said. Telecel Ghana’s sustainability agenda rests on four pillars: Responsible Business, Inclusion for All, Environmental Responsibility, and Sustainable Society. These pillars guide how the organisation manages its operations, deploys technology, supports communities and contributes to Ghana’s sustainable development. Through investments in renewable energy, responsible products, environmental restoration, digital inclusion and employee engagement, Telecel Ghana is working to make sustainability an enduring part of its business and the communities it serves
https://www.myjoyonline.com/telecel-ghan.title_zh: Telecel Ghana在全国ESG峰会上展示务实的气候行动
https://www.myjoyonline.com/telecel-ghan.body_zh:
加纳Telecel以实际行动强化承诺纪念世界可持续发展日，并展示如何将可持续发展融入网络运营、产品、员工文化和社会影响项目。该公司以高级合作伙伴身份参加2026年加纳国家气候与ESG政策峰会，庆祝今年的世界可持续发展日。峰会由Intelligence Nature International组织，在气候变化与可持续发展国务部长办公室支持下举行。峰会汇聚政策制定者、监管机构、发展机构和私营部门领袖，讨论加纳的绿色转型以及企业在加快气候行动方面的作用。

Telecel加纳可持续发展、基金会与对外传播负责人Rita Agyeiwaa Rockson在私营部门专题讨论中呼吁，可持续发展不应只停留在复杂理念和高层承诺上，而应转化为组织、创业者和个人都能理解并采取的实际行动。

Rita表示：“可持续发展不能只是一场只在高层进行的对话，更不能建立在所有人都理解它的假设之上。我们需要简化相关表述，并将其与组织和个人的日常决策联系起来。当人们明白可持续发展如何降低成本、增强韧性以及改善接触客户和投资者的渠道时，它才会真正与他们产生关联。”

她鼓励各组织从可实现的干预措施入手，衡量结果，并利用可信数据推动更宏大的气候目标。Rita补充道：“企业组织、小型企业和个人都可以采取实际行动，为实现我们期望的更大可持续发展目标作出贡献。重要的是迈出第一步、收集数据，并传达由此产生的影响。”

对Telecel加纳而言，这一方针体现在该公司将可持续发展融入各项运营的方式中。为减少运营对环境造成的影响，Telecel加纳正将部分网络基础设施转换为可再生能源，目前已有15个交换局由太阳能供电。这项投资减少了公司对国家电网的依赖，并支持更加可持续的网络运营。

2026年8月，Telecel加纳推出可生物降解的Eco-SIM，其制造过程使用的塑料比标准SIM卡少90%。该组织还在Achimota、Chipa和South Fomangso森林保护地种植了4万多棵树，为再造林和生态系统恢复作出贡献。

其可持续发展工作还延伸至数字普惠和金融普惠。Telecel加纳的服务让客户能够远程完成必要交易，从而减少出行需求、成本及相关排放。其数字普惠项目为创业者，包括女性创办的企业，提供技能和工具，帮助他们提高效率、开拓新市场并增强企业实力。

Rita表示，包容必须继续成为加纳向更绿色经济转型的核心。“在建设未来的社区和经济时，我们必须关注谁正被纳入其中。数字普惠和金融普惠对于确保可持续发展的成果惠及创业者、小型企业和服务不足的社区至关重要。”

在整个活动月期间，Telecel加纳还鼓励员工作出更具环境责任的选择。相关活动包括提倡减少一次性塑料制品的‘无塑料日’，以及把员工与提供环保及本地制造产品的当地创业者连接起来的绿色市场。这些活动表明，日常选择既可以促进负责任消费，也能为推动循环生产的企业创造机会。

该公司参加峰会，将内部活动扩展至围绕气候行动、可持续金融、ESG披露、碳市场和绿色投资的更广泛全国讨论。Rita表示：“我们认识到，可持续发展是一段旅程，仍有更多工作要做。我们的目标十分明确：以支持更具包容性的社会的方式连接人们和组织，同时逐步减少我们的环境影响。实现这一目标需要跨部门协作、实际行动以及持续衡量进展。”

Telecel加纳的可持续发展议程建立在四大支柱之上：负责任业务、人人包容、环境责任和可持续社会。这些支柱指引该组织管理运营、部署技术支持社区并为加纳的可持续发展作出贡献。

通过投资可再生能源、负责任的产品、环境恢复、数字普惠和员工参与，Telecel加纳正努力让可持续发展成为其业务及其所服务社区的一项长期特征
